parts.text:
Meeting: Low-stock alerts and supplier orders – Bakery Brasa (fictional data)
Date: 2026-10-14
Recording part: 1 of 1 (00:00–14:10)
Attendees: Marisol Quiroz (Kitchen manager, stakeholder), Julián Mora (Business analyst), Andrés Gil (Developer), Sofía Rojas (QA)

[00:00:15] Julián: Marisol, you wanted to talk about running out of ingredients.
[00:00:28] Marisol: Twice this month we ran out of butter in the middle of the morning rush and had to stop making croissants. I only notice when the shelf is empty.
[00:01:05] Julián: What would help you notice earlier?
[00:01:12] Marisol: An alert when an ingredient drops below a minimum I set. Per ingredient, because flour and saffron are not the same.
[00:01:50] Andrés: Where would you see the alert?
[00:01:58] Marisol: On the kitchen screen, the one with the order queue. A red badge is enough.
[00:02:30] Sofía: And the minimum, who sets it?
[00:02:36] Marisol: Me and my two assistants. Nobody else should change it.
[00:03:20] Andrés: Stock is only updated when someone counts at the end of the day, so the alert would be a day late.
[00:03:34] Marisol: Then the alert has to use the count we already enter, for now. I would love automatic counts from the supplier invoices, but that is a different project.
[00:03:55] Julián: So for now: minimum per ingredient, red badge on the kitchen screen, based on the daily count. Agreed?
[00:04:02] Marisol: Agreed.
[00:05:40] Marisol: Another thing, the order screen lets customers buy a cake that needs 48 hours' notice with one day's notice. Yesterday we got an order for tomorrow.
[00:05:55] Sofía: I can reproduce that. Choose the custom cake, pick tomorrow as the date and it lets you pay.
[00:06:10] Andrés: It should block the date. The rule is 48 hours, we agreed that on the first of October.
[00:06:20] Marisol: Please fix it this week, I had to call the customer.
[00:06:28] Andrés: I will take it.
[00:08:15] Marisol: Last one. Could the system order butter from the supplier by itself when it is low?
[00:08:25] Andrés: That needs the supplier's API and a budget decision.
[00:08:40] Julián: Let's not commit to that. Marisol, if you want it, ask Finance about the budget and we revisit.
[00:08:50] Marisol: Fine, I will ask Ricardo.

meeting.goals: Marisol Quiroz asked for the meeting because ingredients ran out during the morning rush; the team agreed what a low-stock alert looks like and reviewed an ordering defect.
topics: Butter ran out twice this month during the morning rush and croissants stopped. She only notices when the shelf is empty.
An alert when an ingredient drops below a minimum set per ingredient, shown as a red badge on the kitchen screen with the order queue.
Only the kitchen manager and her two assistants may change it.
Stock is updated only by the end-of-day count, so the alert uses that count and can be a day late. Automatic counts from supplier invoices are a different project.
Cake accepted with too little notice
A cake that needs 48 hours' notice can be paid for with one day's notice. Sofía reproduced it with the custom cake and tomorrow's date. Andrés will fix it this week.
Ordering butter by itself needs the supplier's API and a budget decision. Not committed; Marisol will ask Finance about the budget.
actions: **Andrés Gil:** Block pickup or delivery dates with less than 48 hours' notice for cakes that need it (high).
**Unassigned:** Show a red low-stock badge on the kitchen screen from a minimum set per ingredient (medium).
**Marisol Quiroz:** Ask Ricardo (Finance) about a budget for automatic supplier orders.
decisions: The low-stock alert uses a minimum per ingredient, a red badge on the kitchen screen and the daily count already entered.
Only the kitchen manager and her two assistants can change a minimum.
The 48-hour notice defect is fixed this week.
Automatic supplier ordering is not committed.
related: Risk: The alert is only as current as the end-of-day count, so it can be a day late.
Open question: Who builds the low-stock alert? No owner was named.
Deferred: Automatic stock counts from supplier invoices, a different project.
Deferred: Automatic supplier orders. Needs the supplier's API and a budget decision; Marisol Quiroz will ask Finance.

items.title: Show a low-stock alert on the kitchen screen
items.desc: The kitchen screen shows a red badge for an ingredient whose count is below a minimum set per ingredient. The kitchen manager and her two assistants set the minimums; nobody else can change them. For now the alert uses the daily count already entered, so it can be a day late.
items.notes: 2026-10-14 — Low-stock alert: [Requested by: Marisol Quiroz, after butter ran out twice.] Suggested type: Story — a behaviour the kitchen will see. Risk: based on the end-of-day count, so it can be a day late. No owner was named.
items.ctx: Butter ran out twice this month in the morning rush and croissants stopped. The kitchen manager only noticed when the shelf was empty.
items.story: As the kitchen manager, I want to be alerted when an ingredient falls below its minimum, so that I notice before it runs out.
items.rules: The minimum is set per ingredient. Only the kitchen manager and her two assistants can change it. The alert uses the daily count already entered.
ac: An ingredient's daily count is below the minimum set for it
the kitchen screen shows a red badge for that ingredient
The kitchen manager or one of her assistants sets a minimum for an ingredient
the minimum applies to that ingredient only
A user who is not the kitchen manager or one of her two assistants tries to change a minimum
items.validation: AC1–AC3 are testable and traceable to 00:01:12–00:03:55. No edge case was added because the source supports none; the badge wording and the number of assistants' accounts were not specified.
items.refs: Risk: the alert is only as current as the end-of-day count and can be a day late. Deferred: automatic counts from supplier invoices (00:03:34) and automatic supplier orders (00:08:15), with no commitment.

items.title: Block cake orders with less than 48 hours' notice
items.desc: A cake that needs 48 hours' notice can be ordered and paid for with one day's notice. A customer ordered for the next day and the kitchen had to call them. QA reproduced it with the custom cake and tomorrow's date.
items.notes: 2026-10-14 — Block cakes with less than 48 hours' notice: [Requested by: Marisol Quiroz; reproduced by Sofía Rojas.] Suggested type: Bug — it should block the date and does not. High priority: she asked for the fix this week. Andrés Gil owns it.
items.ctx: The 48-hour rule was agreed on 2026-10-01. Marisol Quiroz received an order for the next day and had to call the customer.
items.expected: The date is blocked because the cake needs 48 hours' notice.
items.current: The order is accepted and the customer can pay.
ac: A customer chooses a cake that needs 48 hours' notice and a date less than 48 hours away
the order cannot be paid for with that date
items.validation: AC1 is testable and traceable to 00:05:55–00:06:20. The source gives no message text or other cake types, so none were invented.
items.refs: Open question: do all cakes need 48 hours' notice or only custom cakes? Only the custom cake was reproduced.
